meta.title: Webhook delivery with retries
meta.description: How a billing platform delivers a signed invoice.paid webhook, retries after a failure and how the receiver checks the signature.

summary.headline: Delivery is at least once: the sender signs and retries until it gets a 2xx, and the receiver verifies, acknowledges fast and processes later.
points: Every attempt is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and the raw body
Any non-2xx answer or a timeout schedules a retry with exponential backoff
The receiver rejects stale timestamps and bad signatures before it trusts the body
The receiver answers 200 at once and does the real work in a background job

facts.Retry schedule: 30 s, 5 min, 30 min, then hourly for 3 days

data.title: Billing service
data.subtitle: Fernway Billing platform
data.description: Marks the invoice as paid and writes the event to an outbox table in the same transaction, so no event is lost if the service stops.

data.title: Delivery queue
data.subtitle: One job per endpoint
data.description: Holds a delivery job for each subscribed endpoint. Retries are scheduled by putting the job back with a delay.

data.title: Webhook dispatcher
data.subtitle: Signs and sends attempts
data.description: Takes a job, signs the payload with the endpoint's secret, posts it and records the response code and latency of every attempt.

data.title: Customer endpoint
data.subtitle: Hollins & Rowe accounts
data.description: Verifies the signature and timestamp, stores the event id to ignore duplicates and hands the work to a background job.

data.title: Background job
data.subtitle: Updates the ledger
data.description: Fetches the invoice from the billing API instead of trusting the body alone, then marks it settled in the customer's ledger.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: An invoice is paid on Fernway. The customer's endpoint is mid-deploy for the first attempt, so the webhook arrives on the second one, 30 seconds later.

steps.title: The event is queued and signed
steps.description: The billing service commits the payment and the outbox event together, and a relay puts one delivery job on the queue. The dispatcher picks it up and signs the timestamp and raw body with the endpoint's secret.

steps.title: The first attempt fails
steps.description: The customer's load balancer answers 503 while new instances start. The dispatcher records the attempt and puts the job back on the queue with a 30-second delay.

steps.title: The retry arrives and is verified
steps.description: The job comes back and is posted again with a fresh timestamp and signature. The endpoint recomputes the HMAC over the raw body, compares it in constant time and rejects timestamps older than five minutes.

steps.title: Acknowledge first, work later
steps.description: The endpoint saves the event id, so a duplicate delivery is ignored, queues a background job and answers 200 within milliseconds. The dispatcher marks the delivery done.

steps.title: The job settles the invoice
steps.description: The background job fetches the invoice from the billing API to get its current state, then marks it settled in the customer's ledger.
